title: fexpr~
description: evaluation of audio signal expressions on a sample by sample basis

arguments.description: expression including operators, functions, inlet types, float and symbols

methods.description: set values for previous input/output values
clear input/output memory, optional symbol specifies a specific input (such as x1) or output (y1)

body:
[fexpr~] evaluates expressions sample by sample with access to previous input and output samples, which makes it a flexible tool for building FIR and IIR filters. It works like [expr] with the addition of $x# for signal inputs and $y# for previous outputs. Inlets are defined by variables of the form $t#, where 't' is the type and # is the inlet number, counting from 1 at the left (up to 100): $f# is a float, $i# is an integer (floats are truncated) and $s# is a symbol, used for array names.

$x# is followed by a sample index in brackets: "$x1[-1]" is the previous sample of the first inlet, and without brackets the current sample is implied, so a filter that averages each sample with the previous one is "fexpr~ ($x1 + $x1[-1])/2". $y# accesses previous output samples of expression #, indexed from -1. Indexes reach back up to the block size (64 by default), and fractional indexes are linearly interpolated.

Multiple expressions separated by semicolons (up to 100) create one outlet each.

Arrays and variables (defined with [value]) are accessed as in C: "tab[5]" is element 5 of the array "tab", "$s2[5]" is element 5 of the array whose name came into inlet 2, and "valx + 10" adds 10 to the [value] named "valx". The store function "=" writes the result of an operation into a variable or array index, as in "tab[$f1] = $f2".

Besides the C operators (arithmetic, relational, bitwise and logical), the available functions are:
math: min, max, int, rint, round, trunc, nearbyint, float, abs, fmod, remainder, floor, ceil, modf, imodf, copysign, ldexp, hypot, if, random, isnan, isinf, finite
power and log: pow, sqrt, cbrt, exp, expm1, ln, log, log10, log1p, fact, erf, erfc
trigonometry: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh
tables: size, sum, Sum, avg, Avg
acoustics: mtof, ftom, dbtorms, rmstodb, dbtopow, powtodb
Functions that output a symbol only work in [expr].
